title: Improving precision scaling via backaction-evading continuous measurement in a driven-dissipative Kerr parametric oscillator
authors: Cheng Zhang, Xinhui Cui, Jiaying Pan, Xin-Qi Li, Mauro Cirio, Pengfei Liang
abstract: Dissipative phase transitions in the driven-dissipative Kerr parametric oscillator offer a promising route for realizing criticality-enhanced quantum sensing based on continuous measurements. However, achieving such enhancement through realistic measurement schemes remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we extend the backaction-evasion strategy introduced in our earlier work for the Gaussian linear case [arXiv:2511.22248 (2025)] to analyze how the quantum and classical Fisher information scale with the Kerr nonlinearity at dissipative critical points. Our results show that backaction-evading homodyne monitoring achieves enhanced photon-number scaling that surpasses the standard quantum limit, and significantly outperforms alternative protocols such as continuous photon counting. As an additional methodological contribution, we also implement and benchmark time-discrete approximation schemes with improved statistical convergence properties. We use these methods to compute the classical Fisher information for continuous homodyne detection, and demonstrate that they provide efficient access to this quantity near dissipative critical points, thereby extending the reach of existing methods.
summary: This paper investigates quantum sensing in a Kerr parametric oscillator by analyzing continuous quantum measurements. It extends backaction-evading measurement techniques to account for Kerr nonlinearity, showing that homodyne monitoring achieves precision scaling beyond the standard quantum limit. The research provides advanced numerical methods for calculating the relevant Fisher information near dissipative critical points.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the precision scaling of quantum sensing by analyzing backaction-evading continuous measurement strategies in a driven-dissipative system.
main_result: Backaction-evading homodyne monitoring surpasses the standard quantum limit in enhancing photon-number scaling and outperforms continuous photon counting protocols.
method: The authors extend the backaction-evasion strategy to include Kerr nonlinearity and develop/benchmark time-discrete approximation schemes for computing the classical Fisher information.
model_or_system: The physical system is a driven-dissipative Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO), which is used as a minimal, experimentally relevant platform for studying quantum critical sensing.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Classical Fisher Information (CFI), and the enhanced photon-number scaling.
important_parameters: Kerr nonlinearity, detection efficiency ($\eta$), and proximity to the dissipative critical point ($\delta	ilde{\epsilon}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis extends previous work from the Gaussian linear case to include finite Kerr nonlinearity, and numerical methods rely on solving stochastic differential equations (SDEs).
figures_summary: Figures compare the classical Fisher information $I_{hd}(\varphi)$ in off-critical regimes and demonstrate the convergence of $I_{hd}(\varphi_{be})$ at the critical point using the Platen scheme.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using Stochastic Master Equations for continuous measurements (homodyne vs. photon counting). It then develops advanced numerical techniques to calculate the Fisher information near critical points, culminating in the demonstration of superior scaling using the backaction-evading homodyne protocol.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum estimation theory in open quantum systems, specifically leveraging non-equilibrium dynamics near critical points, which is highly relevant to modern quantum optics and AMO research.
